newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EC confident Boeing will find remedies for its concerns.
newsitem.headline: EC confident Boeing will find remedies for its concerns.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it was confident that Boeing would come up with adequate changes to its proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas to meet EU concerns.
But it said in a statement that it was up to Boeing, not the Commission, to decide what those remedies were.
"It is not the European Commission's role to identify potential remedies," said a statement read by Willy Helin, spokesman to Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert.
When the Commission raises concerns about a merger, "it is up to the company or companies involved to come up with remedies," it added.

Helin said the Commission was reacting to reported comments by William Baer, a top official at the U.S. Federal Trade Commission about a supposed Commission demand that the merger partners sell Douglas Aircraft.

"The issue raised by director William Baer is but one of the main concerns expressed by the European Commission," the statement said. "We remain confident that Boeing will offer adequate remedies regarding the main competition concerns identified by the Commission.
Helin said the remedies would have to be of a "structural nature".
